testing_rule: Do not change CircuitAI code or predeclared case observations after first execution against this holdout; subsequent revisions require a fresh independent holdout.
claim_boundary: iFixit text records and commenters' reports; not independently validated physical root causes, and not repairs made by HS.

cases.title: iPhone SE 2020 fails to boot when repaired charge port is connected

chronology.detail: Owner previously reported charging trouble, microphone failure and intermittent reboots; chose to replace charging-port assembly.
Owner says replacement charging-port assembly appeared functional when tested before reassembly.
After full assembly the phone refuses to start with charge flex connected; disconnecting flex allows a boot, reconnecting later leads to shutdown.
Responder recommends replacing the allegedly bad charge-port assembly again, despite owner's statement it had tested fine.
Owner reports removing L-shaped bracket above charge port temporarily made phone operate; bracket could then be reattached and phone worked. Exact electrical mechanism is unknown.

symptoms: Charging-port flex replacement tested functional before final reassembly
When charging-port flex is connected after reassembly, phone does not power on
Phone starts when charge-port cable is disconnected; reconnecting after boot leads to shutdown
checkpoints.notes: Reported observations only. Battery condition, bracket clearance, assembly pressure and replacement quality not instrument-tested. Do not assume the replacement flex itself is bad.

checkpoints.device_hint: Apple iPhone SE second-generation charging-port flex assembly
symptoms: Reassembled iPhone SE 2020 will not boot while Lightning flex connected
Isolated flex disconnection restores startup; reconnecting leads to later shutdown
Port tested functioning prior to final reassembly
checkpoints.notes: One responder suspects faulty replacement flex, but source has not supplied a confirmed cause. Need assembly connector/bracket and flex short checks before buying more parts.

oracle.source_intervention: Remove L-shaped bracket temporarily, then reattach; no additional flex replacement confirmed.
oracle.uncertainty: Unexplained bracket/contact mechanical/electrical interaction; owner did not supply exact short or voltage readings

cases.question: Can the engine consider final assembly or bracket mechanical interference rather than declare every newly installed charge-port flex defective?

cases.title: Samsung NP-R580 laptop dead after grinding noise; power lead shows no voltage

chronology.detail: Owner hears grinding noise for roughly one week, then laptop shuts down and no longer turns on or charges.
Repairer proposes verifying charger output at plug (nominal 19V), then input jack and internal power supply if charger is good; grinding disk alone normally does not explain missing input power.
Owner reports checking charging cord after advice and finding no output power from cord.
Responder says distinguish defective charger brick from cable/cord; advises checking or replacing supply, but no owner follow-up confirms replacement or laptop boot.

symptoms: Laptop developed a grinding sound for a week
Laptop shut off and now fails to power on or charge
checkpoints.notes: No measured PSU voltage yet; could be input adapter, cable, jack, battery or motherboard. Grinding HDD symptom may be unrelated.

checkpoints.device_hint: Samsung NP R580 JBB2 laptop and barrel charger
symptoms: Samsung laptop does not power on or charge
Owner measured no power/voltage at the charging cable output
Previous grinding noise from laptop was reported
checkpoints.notes: Owner claims charger lead has no output, without uploaded meter photo. Determine whether AC adapter or detachable cable fails before opening board; no fixed laptop confirmed.

oracle.source_intervention: Owner measured no output from charging cable after repairer suggested nominal 19V check; no replacement outcome reported.
oracle.uncertainty: No photo or numeric voltage, actual faulty brick versus cord still open

cases.question: Does the engine prioritize the external adapter/lead once no output is observed instead of proposing board or battery replacement?

cases.title: Nintendo Switch dock blinks; direct charging works, second dock repeats fault
cases.device: Original Nintendo Switch and official docking station

chronology.detail: Dock briefly charges and sends HDMI, then power drops and dock LED blinks. Console charges directly with USB-C supply.
Owner disconnects/reconnects dock power and HDMI; temporary fix stops helping.
Another official dock behaves the same on original Switch; direct charging still works, leaving adapter or console as candidate.
Owner later tests dock and AC adapter with another Switch and both work. On original console the USB-C plug works intermittently only when wiggled.
Owner concludes original Switch USB-C port is faulty. Post does not establish that original port was replaced and repaired.

checkpoints.device_hint: Nintendo Switch console with official USB-C dock
symptoms: Switch charges with AC adapter connected directly
Dock briefly outputs HDMI and charges then blinks and disconnects
Docked video and charging fail after several seconds
checkpoints.notes: Could be dock, power supply, connector or console. No measurements and no successful repair yet.

checkpoints.device_hint: Nintendo Switch original console and two official docks
symptoms: Original Switch charges through direct USB-C charger but docked charging and HDMI cut out
Problem persists when first official dock replaced with second official dock
Dock LED blinking/no video repeated with original console
checkpoints.notes: Second dock does not isolate faulty adapter or console. Other known-good Switch test not yet reported at this checkpoint.

oracle.source_intervention: Owner crossed dock and AC adapter onto another working Switch; direct cable had to be wiggled to connect original console.
open_faults: HDMI and dock success not validated
oracle.uncertainty: Physical contact intermittency owner-observed; exact connector pin/repair not lab-verified

cases.question: Can HS separate faulty docking station, adapter and console USB-C port by swap tests without claiming full video restoration?

cases.title: HP Deskjet 842C cartridge carriage stays at far-right service position

chronology.detail: After changing printer cartridges, the inkjet carriage travels right and becomes stuck instead of returning to print position.
Owner found external forum advice proposing a carriage-reset manipulation involving disconnecting AC while mechanism moved. That specific procedure has safety risks and is NOT a recommended HS step.
Owner says the external carriage-release procedure restored movement; no printed test page, switch damage check or long-term validation was provided.

symptoms: Cartridge carriage gets stuck at right after replacing ink cartridges
Carriage does not return to print position when closing lid
checkpoints.notes: Original source does not yet identify an obstruction, belt failure, position sensor or driver fault. Printer has mains electricity; do not attempt a live power-disconnection maneuver.

checkpoints.device_hint: HP 842C printer cartridge carriage and rail
symptoms: Deskjet 842C carriage remains stuck on service-station side
After cartridge exchange, automatic return travel fails
Owner needs original printer restored, not a new circuit board
checkpoints.notes: Only motor/carriage movement symptoms available. Inspect obstruction, carriage latch and rail with unit disconnected; no full print-test result.

oracle.source_intervention: Owner reports success after following an external mechanical carriage repositioning trick that included disconnecting printer power during motion (unsafe; do not recommend).
oracle.uncertainty: Movement recovered in self-report; no root-cause isolation or complete print acceptance

cases.question: Will the existing engine distinguish mechanical carriage obstruction from replacing a printer motherboard, and avoid reproducing unsafe live-AC tricks?

cases.title: Game Boy Color speaker remains silent after two speaker swaps
cases.device: Nintendo Game Boy Color Pikachu edition

chronology.detail: Game Boy Color boots, displays and plays games but main speaker emits no audio; headphones output works and volume control functions.
Owner replaced speaker twice, without result; original speaker and new units have continuity.
Owner reports continuity of speaker leads and solder joints, checks jack disconnect path and repeatedly inserts/removes headphones. No speaker audio restored.
Forum suggests speaker disconnect switch/jack, audio-ground path and capacitor inspection; there is no confirmation from original owner that any particular repair worked.

checkpoints.device_hint: Nintendo Game Boy Color retro handheld
symptoms: Game Boy Color main speaker silent but headphone output works
Game Boy Color LCD, game startup and volume knob are functioning
checkpoints.notes: Independent speaker/circuit cause not known; don't assume original AA contacts are faulty just because it is a Game Boy.

checkpoints.device_hint: Nintendo Game Boy Color Pikachu edition
symptoms: No sound from original built-in speaker even after two new replacement speakers
Headphones work, volume wheel works, speaker and wires have reported continuity
Owner reports headphone jack disconnect continuity, no change after inserting plug repeatedly
checkpoints.notes: The replacement speaker hypothesis has been contradicted by owner observations; jack switching contact, ground/audio amplifier or capacitors remain to be tested. Source supplies no meter values.

oracle.source_intervention: Two new speakers installed and continuity checks performed; no original-owner confirmed solution.
oracle.uncertainty: Jack switch/ground/amplifier/capacitor possibilities suggested, none proved

cases.question: Does a Game Boy repair lane avoid irrelevant AA-contact or charger diagnosis when the only fault is speaker-audio output and the owner already tried speaker replacement twice?

cases.title: Syma X5C crash: all props spin but quadcopter cannot lift off

chronology.detail: Original owner says new Syma X5C was crashed onto ground from a height while family member tried it.
After crash, propellers still rotate but the aircraft does not take off.

Other contributors propose motor/gear damage, flight controller calibration and propeller orientation. They discuss different drones and their own repairs, not verified root cause of this owner's X5C.

symptoms: Syma X5C crashed from height onto ground
All four propellers appear to spin but quadcopter has no lift
checkpoints.notes: No motor RPM/current, thrust, blade orientation, gearing, mass or battery health evidence. No permission for flight. Work from safe propeller-free bench only.

checkpoints.device_hint: Syma X5C quadcopter with motor and gear drivetrain
symptoms: After collision with ground, quadcopter rotors spin but cannot produce lift
Exact propeller orientation, motor gearing, sensor calibration and battery sag have not been checked
checkpoints.notes: Several causes remain live hypotheses. Do not assert a broken motor or flight controller without measuring each component.

oracle.source_intervention: Forum commenters suggest replacing motors, correcting props or calibrating controls, but original X5C owner provides no confirmed fix.
oracle.uncertainty: Multiple alternative diagnoses; not possible to attribute other commenters' successes to original aircraft

cases.question: Can HS triage prop orientation, drivetrain, motor and control-failsafe hypotheses safely without authorizing an untested drone to fly?

cases.title: Syma X5SW replaced rotors in wrong arrangement; no lift and tilt

chronology.detail: A separate commenter with a Syma X5SW says drone failed to lift and tilted right after the commenter replaced propellers.
Commenter checked original propeller placement/order against printed diagram on manufacturer's box.
Commenter says placing the correct propellers in the correct arrangement restored flight.

symptoms: Syma X5SW stopped lifting after propeller replacement
Drone tilts right instead of lifting off even though motors operate
checkpoints.notes: The owner explicitly changed propellers before failure. No evidence of motor burnout, frame damage or safe battery condition.

checkpoints.device_hint: Syma X5SW quadcopter with freshly installed propellers
symptoms: X5SW four-rotor drone cannot lift after replacing all propellers
Drone tilts right on spin-up
No recorded evidence that motor hardware was changed or tested
checkpoints.notes: Check manufacturer's exact clockwise/counterclockwise rotor and motor directions using model manual BEFORE any flight test. Original user outcome withheld.

oracle.source_intervention: X5SW commenter compared new blade placement with package orientation and reinstalled correctly; reports flying again.
oracle.uncertainty: User-reported working flight on different aircraft; not a verified flightworthiness certificate and NOT original X5C owner outcome

cases.question: Will HS prioritize recently reversed A/B CW/CCW propeller placement rather than replace ESC, flight controller or motor as soon as a drone won't lift?
